frequency_question: How often does the Reserve Bank of India implement an incremental cash reserve ratio or closely analogous temporary liquidity impounding measure during periods of sudden banking system liquidity surges within a defined horizon?
membership_rule: Members include formal RBI notifications instituting an incremental cash reserve ratio (iCRR) or temporary incremental impounding of deposits. Excluded are standard, permanent changes to the headline Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) or regular variable repo/reverse repo auctions.

cases.name: 2004 Market Stabilization Scheme / iCRR-type liquidity management
2023 iCRR implementation following deposit inflows from banknote withdrawal

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named episodes identified where non-standard incremental ratio tools were deployed to mop up acute liquidity shocks.
known_gaps: Minor variations in terminology or subtle administrative liquidity absorption tools implemented via ad-hoc circulars rather than formal press releases might be undercounted.
skeleton: Three distinct liquidity-surge cycles requiring extraordinary incremental ratio deployment over twenty years of modern central banking operations in this jurisdiction.
multiplier: 3 occurrences across distinct liquidity overhang cycles spanning 20 years, averaging roughly 0.15 per year under specific surplus conditions.
validity_reason: Central banking liquidity management frameworks evolve slowly, and the structural preference for using iCRR as an ad-hoc mop-up tool remains stable across Governor tenures.
